chunks: Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Faddal, from Muhassin ibn Ahmad, and Muhammad ibn al-Walid, and Umar ibn Uthman, and Sindiyy ibn Muhammad, all of them from Yunus ibn Ya'qub, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

And I asked him about the fasting of Sha'ban, so I said to him, 'May I be your ransom, did one of your fathers fast in Sha'ban?' He said, 'The best of my fathers is the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family); his most frequent fasting was in Sha'ban.'
And we have cited a good portion of the narrations regarding the virtue of Sha'ban in our book Al-Kabir.

As for what has been narrated regarding the dislike of fasting in Sha'ban and the prohibition from it, and that none of the Imams (peace be upon them) fasted it, the explanation is that none of the Imams (peace be upon them) fasted it in this specific manner.

Because its fasting is treated like the fasting of the month of Ramadan in terms of obligation and necessity, for some people said that its fasting is obligatory, and Abu al-Khattab, Muhammad ibn Abi Zaynab (may Allah curse him) and his companions went along with this, saying that whoever breaks his fast for one day in it incurs the same expiation as one who breaks his fast for a day in Ramadan.
So criticism came from them (peace be upon them) regarding this, and that none of the Imams (peace be upon them) fasted it in this manner.

And the narrations that included encouragement for separation between the months of Ramadan and Sha'ban, the meaning in them is the prohibition of Sawm al-Wisal (continuous fasting), which we explained in our book Al-Kabir as being forbidden, and it is that one fasts two consecutive days without breaking the fast at night.
And this is indicated by that.

key_terms.أَبُو الْخَطّابِ: Abu al-Khattab, a prominent Shia sect leader
key_terms.صَوْمُ الْوِصَالِ: Continuous fasting without breaking at night
key_terms.صَوْمُ شَعْبَانَ: Fasting in the month of Sha'ban

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on fasting in the month of Sha'ban according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Tusi resolves the apparent contradiction between the encouragement to fast in Sha'ban and the reported dislike by distinguishing between general voluntary fasting and specific innovations, such as Abu al-Khattab’s claim of obligatory status with Ramadan-like expiation. The text clarifies that the prohibition often cited actually targets *Visal* (continuous fasting without breaking the fast at night), a practice the Imams avoided to distinguish their worship from the exaggerated claims of their contemporaries. This highlights the Shia scholarly method of contextualizing narrations to prevent the conflation of recommended acts with obligatory ones or specific historical controversies.
